Subject: Performance SLOs & Private VPC qualification - post-call recap

Hi Samira / Ravi,

Appreciate you taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and next steps for the Private/VPC performance qualification: 

Summary of SLO targets you mentioned on the call:
- P95 latency for text generation (end-to-end) target: <= 200 ms for single-turn queries at 512 tokens.
- Streaming requirement: token-by-token streaming with initial token within 120 ms and sustained per-token latency under 30 ms.
- Throughput target: 300 concurrent sessions (avg 1 request/sec per session) with 1500 rps burst capacity.
- Concurrency: ability to maintain 1,000 concurrent open KV-cached sessions across the pool.

Private/VPC-specific constraints we discussed:
- Network path: you'd prefer VPC peering to avoid egress over the public internet; VPN is ok as fallback for PoC.
- Egress IPs: Acme needs a fixed set of outbound IPs for firewall allowlisting.
- Internal latency budget: app -> gateway -> inference nodes must add <= 120ms; customer-side network hop budget ~40ms.

Actions / next steps (owners):
1) Jordan: share the SLO checklist + network questions (attached). Due: 2026-08-31.
2) Acme (Samira/Ravi): confirm 1) preferred connectivity (Peering vs VPN) and 2) list of CIDRs and existing egress IP requirements. Due: 2026-09-03.
3) Marissa/Neha (Redwood infra): review the proposed concurrency profile and confirm recommended node sizing and expected P95 numbers for the private pool. Due: 2026-09-04.

Questions for your network/security team (please answer when convenient):
- Do you have an existing VPC peering arrangement with any vendors? Any limitations on route table sizes or overlapping CIDRs?
- Are NAT gateways used for egress, and do you require static egress IPs?
- Any MTU constraints, proxy/IDS between app and peered network?

Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist.pdf (SLO checklist + PoC network diagram), proposed-network-diagram.png

Thanks 
we can jump on a 30m technical call next week if your network team wants to go through the diagram live.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake

Jordan - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Connectivity: preference is VPC peering (we want to avoid VPN for steady-state). We'll need Redwood to support a peering model where traffic stays inside the cloud provider backbone.
- Egress/static IPs: we require a set of 4 static egress IPs for our firewalls. If peering doesn't preserve a consistent source IP, we will need a NAT/bastion pattern with fixed egress.
- Latency: our internal app -> edge typically budgets ~30-50ms. The additional path to inference nodes should not exceed 120ms as you noted.
- Streaming: initial token < 150ms would be fine; 120ms is ideal.

We can gather CIDRs and our network contact (Ravi) will provide the details. We can also schedule a technical call next Wed 9/2 at 10am PT if that works for your infra folks.

Thanks,

A couple of additional technical clarifications before the call so we can prep:
- Egress IPs: we can support static egress via NAT gateway in the peered VPC or via a set of proxy egress IPs from our side. Which option is preferred for you (Redwood-managed NAT vs your customer-managed NAT)?
- TLS termination: do you require end-to-end TLS all the way to the container, or is TLS to our edge + mTLS inside the peered network acceptable?
- Connection types: for the PoC can we start with a single peering and fall back to IPsec VPN if we see route flaps?

Marissa / Neha - can you review the requested concurrency/throughput in the SLOs and add rough sizing/comments inline in the attached checklist before the call? High-level notes we discussed on the call: 
- For 300 sustained concurrent sessions and 1500 rps burst, we anticipate a private pool of ~8 x A100-40GB equivalent nodes with continuous batching and KV cache warmed.
- Streaming: to meet initial-token <120ms we recommend enabling low-latency routing and keeping token sizes reasonable on the first 1-2 packets.

Samira/Ravi - attaching the updated SLO checklist (redwood-slo-checklist.pdf) and a proposed network diagram. Please add your CIDRs in the Drive doc linked earlier if you can.

Hi team - quick tech notes ahead of tomorrow's call:

1) Sizing & expected P95 (preliminary, depends on model/seq len):
- With the profile Jordan listed (512 tokens typical, streaming enabled): 8 x A100-40GB equiv => target P95 ~160-220ms depending on model. If you pin a smaller model or enable 4-bit quantized variants we can push P95 down ~20-40ms.

2) Concurrency & KV cache:
- The 1,000 cached sessions is feasible; we'll recommend shard/key affinity to keep warm cache locality. Memory footprint: plan for ~80-120GB of KV cache per node for your profile.

3) Network recommendations:
- VPC peering is preferred. Peering preserves low latency but does not change source IPs inside your VPC; for static egress we can either: 1) put a Redwood-managed NAT in our dedicated VPC that advertises static egress IPs back to you via peering, or 2) you manage NAT on your side and allowlist our pod IP ranges (we'll share ranges). Option 1 is usually simpler for customers who cannot change their own firewall rules frequently.
- MTU/proxies: avoid transparent proxies and traffic inspection between app and peered path - they add variable latency.

4) Streaming behavior:
- To hit initial-token targets we need 3 things: small-ish first-token payloads, low serialization on the customer edge, and the low-latency routing config enabled in the pool. We'll walk through config on the call.

I'll add inline comments to the Drive checklist tonight. See you all on 2026-09-02 at 10am PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Infra Solutions | Redwood Inference
